chain.label: Runway 4L contaminated with compacted snow and ice
chain.trigger: Runway 4L-22R, patches of one inch-deep compacted snow and ice. Runway sanded; friction coefficients averaged 0.32

chain.label: Left crosswind of 10-12 knots with gusts to 22 knots
chain.trigger: wind three three zero at one one... At the approximate time of the takeoff attempt, there were crosswinds of 10-12 knots. Gusts of up to 22 knots were reported

chain.label: Inadequate Tower Air and Boeing B-747 slippery runway procedures permitting early tiller use
chain.trigger: current B-747 operating procedures provide inadequate guidance to flightcrews regarding the potential for loss of directional control at low speeds on slippery runways with the use of the tiller

chain.label: B-747 training simulators lacked slippery runway ground handling fidelity
chain.trigger: the B-747 simulators available for flightcrew training were not capable of adequately simulating the more realistic slippery runway scenarios

chain.label: Inadequate secondary galley latch material/installation for aft galley ice cart
chain.trigger: the material or installation of secondary latches in the galleys of N605FF was inadequate

chain.label: Captain overcontrolled nosewheel steering with progressively larger tiller inputs
chain.trigger: the captain's failure to correct the airplane's deviation from the centerline resulted from his overcontrolling the nosewheel steering through the tiller

caused_by.evidence: overcontrol of the tiller on any aircraft would be more likely on a slippery runway than a dry runway, because airplane heading is less responsive to tiller inputs in slippery conditions

the B-747 has a tendency to react to crosswinds at very slow airspeeds with an initial, slight downwind drift... It would have been natural for the captain to have reacted to this slight deviation with a tiller input
As a result of the Tower Air procedure to guard the tiller during takeoff until 80 knots, the captain was ready to use the tiller during the beginning of the takeoff roll
improved ground handling fidelity of the flight simulators used for B-747 pilot training could have better prepared the captain for handling the situation

chain.label: Nosewheel exceeded critical angle, skidded, and airplane veered left uncontrollably
chain.trigger: the nosewheel quickly exceeded the critical angle at which the traction available for steering was maximized... Further tiller inputs in either direction were ineffective, and the airplane veered to the left in a weathervaning response to the crosswind

caused_by.evidence: excessive nosewheel steering tiller inputs resulted in a loss of directional control on a slippery runway
The simulator responsiveness to tiller inputs was reduced by the slippery runway conditions

chain.label: Captain kept relying on tiller instead of prescribed rudder pedal steering; rudder inputs insufficient or untimely
chain.trigger: the captain of flight 41 first relied on right tiller inputs as the airplane continued to veer left, then applied insufficient or untimely right rudder inputs to effect a recovery

caused_by.evidence: He stated that he added more right rudder and then used the nosewheel steering tiller, but both were ineffective
B-747 procedural information produced by both the airline and the manufacturer permit the tiller to be used at the beginning of the takeoff

chain.label: Captain failed to reject the takeoff in a timely manner
chain.trigger: the captain's failure to reject the takeoff in a timely manner when excessive nosewheel steering tiller inputs resulted in a loss of directional control

caused_by.evidence: instead of rejecting the takeoff immediately after experiencing difficulty obtaining directional control, the captain continued to attempt to regain directional control with progressively greater rudder and nosewheel steering inputs
he applied additional right rudder and tiller steering inputs... before deciding to reject the takeoff
current B-747 flight manual guidance is inadequate about when a pilot should reject a takeoff following some indication of a lack of directional control response
the inadequate fidelity of B-747 flight training simulators for slippery runway operations, contributed to the cause of this accident

chain.label: Captain reapplied forward thrust after retarding power, abandoning the rejected takeoff
chain.trigger: the captain abandoned his attempt to reject the takeoff, at least temporarily, by restoring forward thrust... thrust began to increase to a maximum of 91 percent N1

caused_by.evidence: He said that he then retarded the power levers to idle and applied maximum braking... However, the Safety Board's CVR spectrum analysis clearly indicated that the thrust was partially reduced and then reapplied in significant amounts

chain.label: Airplane departed the left side of runway 4L at about 97 knots
chain.trigger: the LMWLG departed the runway edge... the airspeed was about 97 knots at this time

caused_by.evidence: he had no directional control and that the nose of the airplane continued to turn left... The airplane then departed the left side of the runway
the accident airplane departed the left side of the runway at a relatively high speed (approximately 97 knots)
as a result of the reapplication of thrust, the airplane continued to accelerate as it approached the edge of the runway

chain.label: Airplane struck airfield signs and transformer, collapsing nose gear and separating No. 4 engine; substantial damage
chain.trigger: A 12-foot double-sided sign and two 8-foot single-sided signs were damaged when the airplane hit them after departing the runway. In addition, an FAA-owned transformer was destroyed

caused_by.evidence: The airplane came to rest approximately 4,800 feet from the runway threshold and 600 feet to the left of the runway centerline
this contributed to the severity of the runway excursion and damage to the airplane

chain.label: Aft galley carts broke loose, seriously injuring a flight attendant; 24 passengers minor injuries
chain.trigger: The ice cart hit her right shoulder, and she suffered a broken right shoulder... 24 passengers sustained minor injuries, and a flight attendant received serious injuries

caused_by.evidence: During the airplane's slide, she heard a 'metal sound' in the aft galley, and she saw an ice cart and a beverage cart come loose
the bending in the secondary latches indicated that those latches were engaged, but were not adequate to secure the carts
